body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"siainbuletin"} -->
_Requested by **Sia** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2BWDp9cgemxzr2hZ9jvXJcG)_

Follow-up to #483. After it, `*Messages*` shows `citar preload: ~/Documents/bibliography/a1s1-filosofia-istoriei-viitorului.bib: Wrong type argument: stringp, nil`.

## Merge order

- Base: `main`; no dependency. Touches only `sp-citations` (`.el`, its section in `sp-academic.org`, the preload and layout tests).
- Branch is `claude/project-thread-d7whd6`, not number-prefixed: a cloud session cannot rename a branch after the PR number is known.

## Cause (reproduced on the Mac with the real citar 1.4.0, parsebib 6.7, Emacs 31.1, your 80 `.bib` files)

- It is not a bad entry. The nil is the `format-string` slot of a bibliography that the preload took from `citar-bibliography.eld`.
- `sp-citations-preload--prime` fills `entries`, `props` and `buffers`; `format-string` and the pre-formatted candidates stay nil until `citar-cache--get-bibliography` runs for that file.
- `sp-citations-preload--read` calls `sp-citations--apply-layout` first. In a new session its state is empty, the layout counts as changed, and `sp-citations--repreformat` pre-formatted every bibliography in the cache, including the primed ones. `citar-format--parse` fails on a nil format string.
- The file in the message is only the first in hash order; any primed file would fail. The preload took it for "saved entries did not work", dropped that file and read it again, so the cost was one wasted parse and a misleading message.
- With an empty cache (first pass) or a second pass in the same session nothing is primed or the state is set, which is why the tests did not see it.

## Changes

- `sp-citations--repreformat` skips a bibliography without a format string (`citar-cache--get-bibliography` sets it and pre-formats the file itself). Checked on the Mac in a scratch copy: the primed pass then ran with no error and no re-parse.
- From the first commit of this PR, kept for other errors: the backtrace of a preload error (`M-x sp-citations-preload-show-error`), a retry from the `.bib` when saved entries fail, and an error in one file no longer stops the other files.
- Docs as bullets; no CHANGELOG edit; no `when-let`.

## Timings (batch, your real files, 80 `.bib`, sum over all files)

- First parse without a cache: 1.4 to 1.6 s (slowest: `humanities.bib` 0.33 s, `marx.bib` 0.29 s, `a1s1-filosofia` 0.09 s).
- Primed read from the disk cache: 0.4 to 0.8 s. The cache file is about 11.7 MB.

## Tested

- On the Mac, batch Emacs 31.1 with the real citar: the error reproduced from a copy of your live cache; the fix removed it (scratch copy).
- Here (Emacs 29.3, stand-in for `citar-cache`): `tests/sp-citations-preload-test.el` 16 pass, `tests/sp-citations-layout-test.el` 13 pass, also when loaded together. New: `sp-citations-repreformat-skips-bibliographies-from-the-disk`, which signals like citar on a nil format string.
- `tools/check-tangle.sh`: the `.el` matches the doc.

## Not tested

- A graphical frame: the real frame width, the pixel-cell path and the idle-timer flow in a running Emacs.
- Your live session with this branch.

## Manual testing

- [x] `cd ~/dotfiles; git fetch origin claude/project-thread-d7whd6; git checkout claude/project-thread-d7whd6`, restart Emacs, wait for the idle pass
- [x] `*Messages*` ends with `citar preload: N bibliography file(s) ready` and has no `citar preload:` error line
- [x] `M-x sp-citations-preload-explain`: every file says `ready`
- [x] `M-x citar-open`: no `Updating bibliography`, no wait
- [x] Restart again: no error, no `Updating` lines
- [x] `M-x sp-citations-fit-layout` and resize the frame: candidates still look right

<details><summary>Revert after testing</summary>

- `git -C ~/dotfiles restore .`, then `git -C ~/dotfiles switch main && git -C ~/dotfiles pull`; restart Emacs.
- Delete `citar-bibliography.eld` in your cache dir for a cold start.

</details>

commit.message:
🐛 Keep the backtrace of a citar preload error and recover from bad saved entries

The preload stopped on the first file with "Wrong type argument: stringp,
nil" after the disk cache was used. Keep the backtrace for
sp-citations-preload-show-error, read a file again when its saved entries
fail, and go on with the next file after an error.

commit.message:
🐛 Skip bibliographies without a format string when the layout is applied again

In a new session the preload put entries from the disk cache into citar's
cache; sp-citations--apply-layout then pre-formatted every bibliography,
and citar-format--parse failed on the nil format string of those. Found by
running the preload against the real citar 1.4.0.
